definition: A 27B Qwen3.5 model, used across 4 sources as a mid-large open backbone. Its archived appearances: as one of three backbones for a diagnosis-guided recovery harness, where it goes from 56.90 to 94.90 percent on an embodied benchmark and shows the pattern of a stronger base narrowing the margin; as a latent safety guard whose 268.56 rationale tokens compress to 1.60 with an 8.9-fold speedup; as the open-weight model that outperforms commercial systems on financial advice under a causal-effect evaluation; and in claim-level reliability assessment.

evidence.note: Compresses a safety guard's textual rationales into continuous latent states by a staged curriculum, cutting 268 reasoning tokens to 1.60 and latency 8.9-fold, and adds an on-demand decoder that reconstructs a human-readable audit artifact — whose own ablation shows the artifact is anchored far more by the source text than by the latent states it is supposed to inspect.
evidence.title: LatentGuard: Efficient and Inspectable Latent Reasoning for LLM Safeguards

evidence.note: Profiles the dominant failure mode of an agent task family on development data, then freezes a policy that permits only the recovery interventions matched to that failure -- so a failure decides which repair is admissible and how much evidence to spend, rather than triggering more context indiscriminately.
evidence.title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction

evidence.note: Trains an open-weight model with GRPO against a safety-gated LLM-as-a-judge rubric for financial advice, then audits the result with a judge-independent causal estimator on logged outcomes -- and finds the two evaluations rank the other systems differently, with the untrained base model last on the rubric and second on the audit.
evidence.title: GRPO for Financial Advice Generation: Outperforming Commercial LLMs under CATE Evaluation

evidence.note: Reallocates half of a test-time sampling budget from generating more solutions to asking the same model to refute a handful of decision-critical claims extracted from each trace, then weights the consensus vote by how many claims survive.
evidence.title: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

name: Qwen3.5-27B
